title: Friends of the Earth (No. 3): A Tale of Two Statutory Interpretations
content:
Abstract
The High Court in Friends of the Earth (No. 3), delivered on the 25th of October 2024, a decision which concerned the statutory interpretation of section 58 of the Climate Change Act 2008 (‘CCA’) that obliges the Secretary of State to issue a programme for adaption to climate change, including setting out the government’s objectives, proposals and policies in this regard. The claimants relied on the High Court’s earlier findings in Friends of the Earth (Nos. 1 and 2) that saw the government’s Net Zero Strategy and Carbon Budget Delivery Plan, which were similarly prepared pursuant to the CCA, declared unlawful. However, the High Court in Friends of the Earth (No. 3) found that the duties in the CCA for climate mitigation—interpreted in Friends of the Earth (Nos. 1 and 2)—and those for climate adaptation are held to different standards. Following from this, it found that the government’s National Adaptation Programme 3 (‘NAP3’) was lawful. In this analysis, I argue that the High Court’s legal reasoning in this respect overstates the difference between climate mitigation and adaptation plans as found in the CCA. In doing so, it fails to recognise important synergies between climate mitigation and adaptation, which are both essential in addressing climate change.
